question: A new Linux EC2 server has no password at all. Amazon only gives you a .pem key file when the server is created. Should the "Authorize on Server" step let the user pick a saved .pem file instead of typing a password?
optionLabel: Yes: choose either a password or a saved .pem file

question: Where should saved .pem files live in ShipRight? Today the Resources page has a Credentials tab, but those are Git logins (a name, a secret value and a host such as github.com).
optionLabel: A new "Key files" tab on the Resources page

question: On an EC2 server there is no password to type — Amazon only gave the user a .pem key file when the server was created. What should the help tooltip next to the Authorize step tell them to do?
optionLabel: Send them to their .pem file (EC2 has no password)

question:
In a server's settings a signed-in member of a company can have ShipRight generate and manage one Ed25519 key for that server, then authorize it once on the server so ShipRight is never prompted again. Because cloud servers such as a new Linux EC2 instance have no server password (Amazon only gives a .pem key file at creation), the Authorize step lets the user either type a password or pick a saved .pem key file, and a step-by-step help tip next to the step explains the EC2 case. To make .pem files re-usable, the company can store them as shared resources in a new "Key files" tab on the Resources page. This version covers EC2 only; other cloud providers come later.
